grammar_notes.title: Talking About the Past ('akaiswa')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'akaiswa' expresses a completed past action. Shona has two main ways to talk about the past: 1) For actions that happened earlier today or very recently, combine the short subject prefix ('nda-' = I, 'wa-' = you, 'a-' = he/she, 'ta-' = we, 'va-' = they) directly with the verb stem (e.g., 'ndamuka' = 'I woke up today', 'wabudirira' = 'you have succeeded'). 2) For events that happened yesterday or further in the past, insert '-ka-' after the subject prefix (e.g., 'takatenga' = 'we bought', 'vakaenda' = 'they went', 'akadanidzira' = 'he shouted').
grammar_notes.rule: Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

grammar_notes.title: Colours & Describing Objects in Shona ('aneruvara')
grammar_notes.content: This passage uses colour vocabulary such as 'aneruvara'. Shona has three traditional core colour adjectives that change their prefix slightly to match the noun they describe: '-chena' (white/clean, e.g., 'ruvara ruchena' or 'shangu chena'), '-tema / nhema' (black/dark, e.g., 'mota nhema' or 'ruvara rutema'), and '-tsvuku' (red/bright brown, e.g., 'mota tsvuku' or 'ruvara rutsvuku'). For other colours like green ('girinhi'), blue ('bhuruu'), or orange ('orenji'), speakers typically say 'ruvara rwe-' ('the colour of...') followed by the colour name, as in 'ruvara rwegirinhi' (green).
grammar_notes.rule: Core Colours: -chena (white), -tema / nhema (black), -tsvuku (red) | Phrase pattern: ruvara rwe-[colour] (e.g., ruvara rwegirinhi)

grammar_notes.title: Joining Words with 'ne-' ('and / with') in 'nemasofa'
grammar_notes.content: Look closely at 'nemasofa'. In Shona, the word for 'and' or 'with' between nouns is not a separate word—instead, the prefix 'ne-' (or 'na-' before people's names) is written attached directly to the second noun! For example, 'ne-' + 'masofa' forms 'nemasofa'. You will see this everywhere in daily speech: 'sadza nemuriwo' ('sadza and vegetables'), 'nesimba' ('with strength'), and 'nekukasira' ('with haste / quickly').
grammar_notes.rule: ne- + Noun = and / with [Noun] (written as a single word, e.g., sadza nemuriwo = sadza and vegetables)

cultural_notes.title: Local Upholstery & Roadside Furniture Workshops ('Masofa Nemadhizaini')
cultural_notes.content: In suburbs like Glen View in Harare, skilled local carpenters and upholsterers craft custom lounge suites ('masofa ane madhizaini') that are displayed outdoors for buyers across the country.

Which bus goes to the city centre?

active_exercises.explanation: 'Mukoma wangu' = 'My older brother', 'akatenga' = 'bought', 'mota chena' = 'a white car', 'nezuro' = 'yesterday'.
